definition_zh: 建立；创立；创办（find 的过去式、过去分词：找到）
definition_en: to start or establish something such as a school, company, or city
core_image: 往地里打下第一根桩：建筑、组织从这一刻立起来
scene: 校庆典礼上，老校友指着石碑讲起学校的起源。 The school was founded more than eighty years ago.
sceneCN: 这里 found 是「创立」的意思（第 1 个义项：创办机构）；学校是八十多年前建立的。

collocations.zh: 创立于二十世纪九十年代的慈善机构

derivatives.zh: found 加 -er，义为「创始人；创立者」（另义「沉没」的 founder 是不同动词）
义为「基础；地基；基金会；创立」
foundation 加 -al，义为「基础的；根本的」
co- + founder，义为「共同创始人」

senses.title: To establish an organization or place
senses.definition: to bring an institution, company, or city into existence
senses.definitionCN: 使机构、公司或城市开始存在。
senses.example: Her grandfather founded a small hospital in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父在镇上创办了一家小医院。
senses.why: The Latin fundare meant to lay a bottom or base, and founding is laying the first base of an organization.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fundare 意为「打基础」，创立组织就是给它打第一层地基。

senses.title: To base something on a principle
senses.definition: to base a belief, action, or decision on something
senses.definitionCN: 让信念、行动或决定以某物为依据。
senses.example: The verdict was founded on solid evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 判决建立在确凿的证据之上。
senses.why: The base image works for ideas as well as buildings.
senses.whyCN: 地基意象同样适用于抽象的观念。

senses.title: Past form of find
senses.titleCN: find 的过去式与过去分词
senses.definition: the past and participle of find, meaning discovered
senses.definitionCN: find 的过去式/过去分词，表示「找到」。
senses.example: I found my lost pen under the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 我在桌子底下找到了丢的钢笔。
senses.why: This is a different verb: find, found, found, sharing the shape but not the origin.
senses.whyCN: 这是另一个动词 find 的变形，与「创立」的 found 同形不同源。

intro.en: Found the verb to establish and found the past of find are two separate words that only look alike.
intro.cn: 「创立」的 found 与 find 的过去式 found 是两个词源完全不同的词，只是外形相同。

items.en: Fundare meant to lay a bottom, from fundus, the bottom or base.
items.cn: fundare 意为「打基础」，来自 fundus（底、基础）。

items.en: The word entered Old French as fonder, used for founding churches and cities.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语作 fonder，用于创建教堂与城市。

items.en: English borrowed fonden in the thirteenth century for establishing institutions.
items.cn: 英语十三世纪借入 fonden，用于创立机构。

items.en: Separately, the verb findan (to come upon) had the past form funde, ancestor of the other found.
items.cn: 另一边，古英语动词 findan（碰上、发现）的过去式 funde 是「找到」义 found 的祖先。

items.en: The two words merged in spelling but kept their different families: founder, foundation versus find, finder.
items.cn: 两词拼写合一但词族分明：founder、foundation 属一方，find、finder 属另一方。

note.en: Words that look like found and words about beginnings and bases.
note.cn: 与 found 形近的词及表示起点、根基的词。

entries.definition: a person who establishes something; also a verb meaning to sink or fail
entries.definitionCN: 创始人；另有「沉没、失败」义的动词，是同形不同源词。

entries.definition: a sum of money set aside; from Latin fundus, related to founding
entries.definitionCN: 基金；资金；与 found 同出拉丁 fundus。

entries.definition: a factory where metal is cast; from French fonderie
entries.definitionCN: 铸造厂；来自法语 fonderie，属同根词。

entries.definition: to set up permanently
entries.definitionCN: 设立；建立；与 found 的创办义近义。

entries.definition: to start a business or organization
to start or introduce a system or rule

normalIntro.en: Five hooks separating the two founds and fixing the founder family.
normalIntro.cn: 区分两个 found 并锚定 founder 词族的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Found (create) comes from Latin fundus, the bottom: you lay the base first.
normal.cn: 创立义的 found 出自拉丁 fundus（底）：先打地基再建楼。

normal.en: The other found is simply find in the past: find, found, found.
normal.cn: 另一个 found 就是 find 的过去式：find、found、found。

normal.en: Foundation has three faces: base, establishment, and charity fund.
normal.cn: foundation 一词三面：地基、创立、基金会。

normal.en: A founder is one who lays the base of a company.
normal.cn: founder 就是给公司「打地基」的人。

normal.en: Be founded on means built on a principle, like a building on stone.
normal.cn: be founded on 指以某原则为基础，如楼立于石。

abstract.en: Picture a builder hammering the first stake into soil.
abstract.cn: 想象建造者把第一根桩打进土里。

abstract.en: Picture a stone foundation under a rising school gate.
abstract.cn: 想象校门下方正在垒砌的石头地基。

abstract.en: Picture hands brushing dust off a found wallet.
abstract.cn: 想象双手拂去拾获钱包上的灰尘。

examples.en: The charity was founded by a group of retired teachers.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构由一群退休教师创办。

examples.en: Their friendship is founded on many years of trust.
examples.cn: 他们的友谊建立在多年的信任之上。

examples.en: She found the ticket she thought she had lost.
examples.cn: 她找到了本以为丢了的那张票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「防倒的」——地基打得好才能防倒：found 创立，先立防倒的根基。

root: found（创立）来自拉丁语 fundare「打基础」，词根 fundus「底」；经古法语 fonder 进入英语。与 find 的过去式 found 仅同形不同源。同根词：foundation（基础）、founder（创始人）、fund（资金）。

sensesIntro.en: Found moves from laying a physical base to establishing institutions and abstract bases, beside its twin past of find.
sensesIntro.cn: found 从「打地基」到「创办机构」，再到「抽象根基」；旁边还站着同形的 find 过去式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first stone laid under everything that follows
core.cn: 核心意象：垫在一切之上的第一块石头

branches.en: Starting a school, company, or city
branches.cn: 创办学校、公司或城市

branches.en: The person who lays the base is the founder
branches.cn: 打地基的人即创始人

branches.en: Ideas stand on evidence as on stone
branches.cn: 观念立于证据，如楼立于石

branches.en: Decisions founded on principles
branches.cn: 决定以原则为根基

branches.en: The unrelated twin: past of find
branches.cn: 无关的孪生词：find 的过去式

intro.en: Found heads a Latin family about bottoms, bases, and beginnings.
intro.cn: found 统领一个关于「底、基、始」的拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: The root fundus gives English both the establish family and the money family.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 fundus 在英语中同时衍生「创立」族与「资金」族。

items.example: The fundus of a cup is its base.
They found a new club this year.
The founder opened the first shop.
He asked for a full refund.
She is the co-founder of the app.

items.meaning: place where metal is founded or cast
items.example: Iron was melted in the foundry.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 底；基础；（作为基底的）田产

latinEntries.meaning: to lay a bottom or foundation

definition_zh: 票；入场券；罚单；（政党）候选人名单
definition_en: a piece of paper or a digital pass that gives you the right to travel, enter or attend something
core_image: 一张印着几行小字的小纸片，检票口看一眼就放行
scene: 出门赶车前他忽然在口袋里翻找,怕那张小纸片弄丢了。 She checked her pocket twice to make sure the ticket was still there.
sceneCN: 这里 ticket 是「车票」（第 1 个义项：凭以乘车的小票据）；句意为她摸了两次口袋，确认车票还在。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「售票；开罚单」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「持票的；被开罚单的」
由 ticket 与 holder 复合，义为「持票人」

senses.title: A pass for travel or entry
senses.definition: a printed or digital piece of evidence giving the holder the right to travel or enter
senses.definitionCN: 纸质或电子凭证，持者有乘车或入场的权利
senses.example: Two return tickets to the city, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请给我两张到城里的往返票。
senses.why: The word began as a written note, and a note is enough to pass a gate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是一张书面便条，而一张便条足以通过一道闸。

senses.title: A notice of a fine
senses.definition: an official notice that you must pay a fine for a traffic or parking offence
senses.definitionCN: 因交通或停车违章而须缴纳罚款的正式通知
senses.example: There was a parking ticket under the windscreen wiper.
senses.exampleCN: 雨刷下夹着一张违章停车罚单。
senses.why: The right to pass became a right to punish: the same slip of paper, in another colour.
senses.whyCN: 「准予通行」变成了「予以处罚」：同一张小纸片，换了个颜色。

senses.title: A means to an end
senses.definition: in phrases such as a ticket to success, the thing that enables you to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a ticket to success 一类短语，指使人达到目标的手段
senses.example: Fluent English was her ticket to a better job.
senses.exampleCN: 流利的英语是她得到更好工作的门径。
senses.why: Whatever lets you through a door is a ticket, even when it is not paper.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能让你通过一道门的东西都是 ticket，即使它不是纸。

senses.title: A political list of candidates
senses.definition: the list of candidates that a party puts forward in an election
senses.definitionCN: 政党在选举中推出的候选人名单
senses.example: He won a place on the party ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢得了该党名单上的一个位置。
senses.why: Candidates travel on one list as passengers travel on one ticket.
senses.whyCN: 候选人同上一个名单，就像乘客凭同一张票同行。

intro.en: Ticket came into English from French, where it began as a short note rather than a travel pass.
intro.cn: ticket 经法语进入英语，最初指一张短小的便条，而非车票。

items.en: Old French estiquet meant a note or a label, something stuck onto a document or a door.
items.cn: 古法语 estiquet 意为便条或标签，是贴在文书或门上的东西。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word as ticket, and it named a written note, a licence or a short record.
items.cn: 中古英语借入作 ticket，指书面便条、许可证或简短记录。

items.en: By the seventeenth century ticket had become the slip that admits you to a coach, a play or a lottery draw.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，ticket 已指让人乘车、看戏或抽签的凭据。

items.en: The nineteenth century added the police sense, the ticket that charges rather than admits.
items.cn: 十九世纪增添了警察用法：不再放行而是处罚的票单。

items.en: Modern English made tickets digital, but the word still means the right to go through.
items.cn: 现代英语让票数字化了，但这个词仍表示「可以过去」的权利。

note.en: The first group separates ticket from near spellings; the second compares passes, vouchers and fines.
note.cn: 第一组区分 ticket 与形近词；第二组比较票证、凭单与罚款。

entries.definition: A check mark, or a small insect; one syllable less and another root.
entries.definitionCN: 勾；蜱虫（少一个音节，词源不同）

entries.definition: To touch lightly and make someone laugh.
The rise and fall of the sea; a different root entirely.
An adhesive label, literally a thing stuck on.
entries.definitionCN: 贴纸（同源，本义「贴上去的东西」）

entries.definition: A card or document that lets you enter freely, often repeatedly.
A printed piece of paper exchangeable for goods or money.
The money paid for a journey, not the paper itself.
Money paid as a penalty; the ticket is only the notice of it.
entries.definitionCN: 罚款（票只是通知，钱才是罚）

normalIntro.en: Hooks from the short-note origin and the two opposite jobs of the same slip.
normalIntro.cn: 钩子来自「便条」的来源，以及同一纸片两种相反的职责。

normal.en: Ticket began as a little note, and a note still gets you through a gate.
normal.cn: ticket 最初是一张小便条，而一张便条仍能让你过闸。

normal.en: A travel ticket lets you go; a parking ticket stops you with a fine.
normal.cn: 车票放你过去，罚单则用罚款拦住你。

normal.en: Ticket office is where you pay before, the ticket machine where you pay quickly.
normal.cn: ticket office 是提前买票的地方，ticket machine 是快速买票的机器。

normal.en: A ticket to success is not paper; it is whatever opens the door.
normal.cn: 通往成功的 ticket 不是纸，而是任何能开门的凭据。

normal.en: Do not mix it with tick or tide: check the middle letters.
normal.cn: 不要与 tick 或 tide 混：看清中间的字母。

abstract.en: Picture a small slip flicked across a counter, the one thing that decides whether you pass.
abstract.cn: 想象一张小纸片从柜台那头弹过来，它单单决定你能不能过去。

abstract.en: The word is a legal token: it carries permission in miniature.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一枚微型的法律凭证，把许可装在小尺寸里。

abstract.en: The same paper can open a door or close a bank account.
abstract.cn: 同一张纸可以打开一扇门，也可以掏空一个账户。

examples.en: I booked two tickets for the evening train.
examples.cn: 我订了两张晚班火车的票。

examples.en: He got a ticket for parking on the pavement.
examples.cn: 他因为人行道上停车被开了罚单。

examples.en: Good writing is still a ticket to better work.
examples.cn: 好文笔仍是通往更好工作的门径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「替课特」——替人上课特批一张凭条 → ticket 票

root: 古法语 estiquet「便条、标签」，中古英语借入为 ticket，本指书面便条或许可；十七世纪转指乘车看戏的凭据，十九世纪又衍生出交警罚单义。

sensesIntro.en: Ticket is a small slip that carries permission, and the same shape of paper can also carry a penalty, a career chance or a party list.
sensesIntro.cn: ticket 是一张承载许可的小纸片，同一形状的纸也能承载罚款、职业机会或政党名单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small slip flicked across a counter that decides whether you pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从柜台弹来的小纸片，决定你能不能过去。

branches.en: The pass: permission in miniature.
branches.cn: 通行线：微缩的许可。

branches.en: The fine: the same slip turned against you.
branches.cn: 罚款线：同一纸片反过来对付你。

branches.en: The chance: whatever opens a door.
branches.cn: 机会线：任何能开门的凭据。

branches.en: The list: candidates travelling together on one ballot.
branches.cn: 名单线：候选人共用一张选票同行。

branches.en: Two opposite powers share one small piece of paper.
branches.cn: 两种相反的权力共住一张小纸片。

intro.en: Ticket takes -s, -ed and -ing; it compounds with office, holder and machine.
intro.cn: ticket 可加 -s、-ed、-ing，并与 office、holder、machine 复合。

latinIntro.en: The stem came through French from an old root for sticking, with no Latin entry needed here.
latinIntro.cn: 词干经法语而来，源出表示「粘贴」的古老词根，此处无需拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 满意；满足；履行；补偿
definition_en: a feeling of pleasure when a need or hope is met; the fulfilment of a demand or obligation; compensation for a wrong
core_image: 一个空杯子被倒满，心里也随之安稳
scene: 她对考试结果很满意。 She felt great satisfaction with her exam results.
sceneCN: 这里 satisfaction 是「满意、满足」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她对考试结果很满意。

forms.label: 复数（指具体的满足或补偿）

derivatives.zh: 使满意；满足
感到满意的
令人满意的

senses.title: Contentment
senses.definition: a feeling of pleasure when a need or hope is met
senses.definitionCN: 需要或希望得到满足时的愉快感受
senses.example: She smiled with satisfaction.
senses.exampleCN: 她满意地笑了。
senses.why: The core sense is the good feeling of having enough.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是「足够」带来的良好感受。

senses.title: Fulfilment of a claim
senses.definition: the act of fulfilling a demand, duty, or debt
senses.definitionCN: 满足要求、履行职责或清偿债务的行为
senses.example: The company worked for the satisfaction of all claims.
senses.exampleCN: 公司努力清偿所有索赔。
senses.why: The feeling of enough extends to settling what is owed.
senses.whyCN: 「足够」的感受延伸到结清所欠之物。

senses.title: Compensation
senses.definition: something given to make up for a wrong or injury
senses.definitionCN: 为弥补过错或伤害而给予的东西
senses.example: He demanded satisfaction for the insult.
senses.exampleCN: 他要求为受辱获得补偿。
senses.why: An old legal sense treats a wrong as a debt to be paid.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律义把过错视为需要偿还的债。

intro.en: Satisfaction comes from Latin satisfactio, from satis enough and facere to make.
intro.cn: satisfaction 来自拉丁语 satisfactio，由 satis（足够）与 facere（做）构成。

items.en: Satis means enough.
items.cn: satis 意为足够。

items.en: Facere means to make or do.
items.cn: facere 意为做或制造。

items.en: Satisfactio means making amends.
items.cn: satisfactio 意为作出补偿。

items.en: The word enters French legal use.
items.cn: 该词进入法语法律用语。

items.en: It names both contentment and compensation.
items.cn: 现代英语中它兼指满意与补偿。

note.en: Satisfaction is the feeling of enough; saturation means being full to the limit.
note.cn: satisfaction 是满足感，saturation 则是达到饱和。

entries.definition: the state of being completely full
approval or a penalty
a feeling of not being pleased
quiet happiness with what one has
the achievement of a need or aim
pleasure from satisfying a desire

normalIntro.en: Satisfaction is what you feel when something is finally enough.
normalIntro.cn: satisfaction 就是事情终于「足够」时的感受。

normal.en: She looked at the finished work with satisfaction.
normal.cn: 她满意地看着完成的作品。

normal.en: Customer satisfaction has risen this year.
normal.cn: 今年顾客满意度上升了。

normal.en: The matter was settled to everyone's satisfaction.
normal.cn: 这件事以人人满意的方式解决了。

normal.en: He gets great satisfaction from teaching.
normal.cn: 他从教学中获得极大满足。

normal.en: The court demanded satisfaction of the debt.
normal.cn: 法院要求清偿这笔债务。

abstract.en: Picture an empty cup filled to the brim.
abstract.cn: 想象一个空杯被倒到杯沿。

abstract.en: Imagine a debt crossed out at last.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债务终于被划掉。

abstract.en: Think of a wrong balanced by a fair payment.
abstract.cn: 把过错想成由公平偿付来平衡。

examples.en: He nodded in satisfaction at the result.
examples.cn: 他对结果满意地点了点头。

examples.en: The workers expressed satisfaction with the new rules.
examples.cn: 工人们对新规定表示满意。

examples.en: The injured party sought satisfaction in court.
examples.cn: 受害方在法庭上寻求补偿。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 拉丁组合
dict_mnemonic.text: satis（足够）+ factio（做）= satisfaction，把该做的做到足够，就有了「满足」。

root: satisfaction 源自拉丁语 satisfactio，由 satis（足够）与 facere（做）组合，原义为「做到足够、作出补偿」。

sensesIntro.en: Satisfaction is contentment, the fulfilment of a claim, or compensation for a wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: satisfaction 指满足感、对要求或债务的履行，或对过错的补偿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup filled to the brim and set at rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子被倒满，安然放下。

branches.en: The base sense is the feeling of enough.
branches.cn: 基础义是「足够」带来的感受。

branches.en: Enough turns into fulfilling what is owed.
branches.cn: 「足够」转化为履行所欠之物。

branches.en: A wrong becomes a debt to be paid.
branches.cn: 过错被看作需要偿还的债。

branches.en: Settling a claim brings contentment.
branches.cn: 清偿索赔带来满足感。

branches.en: Fulfilment and compensation both close an obligation.
branches.cn: 履行与补偿都了结一项义务。

intro.en: Satisfaction belongs to the satisf- family built on satis and facere.
intro.cn: satisfaction 属于由 satis 与 facere 构成的 satisf- 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin satis, facere, and satisfacere explain satisfaction and satisfy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 satis、facere 与 satisfacere 解释了 satisfaction 与 satisfy。

items.exampleCN: 这顿饭让每个人都很满足。
这是一顿令人满足的饭。

latinEntries.exampleCN: satis 是 satisfaction 的开头。

definition_zh: 借入；借用；借钱；借用（词语、想法）
definition_en: to take something from someone with the intention of giving it back
core_image: 从朋友手里接过一本书，答应下周归还
scene: 图书馆的柜台前，学生把借书卡递过去，接过一本厚重的词典。 She borrowed a dictionary from the library.
sceneCN: 这里 borrow 是「借入」（第 1 个义项：拿走某物并打算归还）；句意为她从图书馆借了一本词典。

senses.title: To take and return
senses.definition: to take something from someone and agree to give it back later
senses.definitionCN: 从别人那里拿走某物，并约定以后归还
senses.example: Can I borrow your pen for a moment?
senses.exampleCN: 我能借你的笔用一下吗？
senses.why: Old English borgian meant to take on pledge, and a borrowed thing is held on the promise to return it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 borgian 意为以担保方式取得，借来的东西是在归还的许诺下持有的。

senses.title: To take money on loan
senses.definition: to take money from a person or bank and agree to pay it back
senses.definitionCN: 从个人或银行取得钱款，并约定偿还
senses.example: They borrowed money to buy the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借钱买了房子。
senses.why: Money borrowing is the same promise in a heavier form: the pledge now includes interest.
senses.whyCN: 借钱是同一个许诺在更重的形式下的版本：担保里如今还包括利息。

senses.title: To take words or ideas
senses.definition: to take a word, idea or custom from another language or group
senses.definitionCN: 从另一种语言或群体取用词语、想法或习俗
senses.example: English borrowed many words from French.
senses.exampleCN: 英语从法语借用了许多词。
senses.why: A borrowed word is taken into a new language and, in a sense, never given back, which is why languages borrow too.
senses.whyCN: 借词被取进另一种语言，某种意义上再也不归还，所以语言之间也会「借」。

intro.en: Borrow comes from an old word for a pledge, and the promise to return is still inside it.
intro.cn: borrow 来自表示「担保」的古词，归还的许诺至今仍在这个词里。

items.en: Old English borgian meant to borrow or to lend, both resting on a pledge between two people.
items.cn: 古英语 borgian 既表示借入也表示借出，两者都建立在两人之间的担保上。

items.en: The noun borg meant a pledge or security, the thing that made a loan safe.
items.cn: 名词 borg 意为担保或抵押，是让借贷变得安全的凭据。

items.en: German borgen and Dutch borgen are relatives, both covering borrowing and lending.
items.cn: 德语 borgen 与荷兰语 borgen 是同源词，都兼指借入与借出。

items.en: The word was applied to languages, so a word taken from another tongue is a borrowing.
items.cn: 这个词也被用到语言上，于是从别的语言取来的词就叫借词。

items.en: Today borrow covers objects, money and words or ideas taken from others.
items.cn: 今天 borrow 覆盖物品、钱款以及取用他人的词语或想法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects words about lending and taking.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收与借贷、取用有关的词。

normal.en: Old English borgian rested on borg, a pledge, and a loan is still a promise.
normal.cn: 古英语 borgian 建立在 borg（担保）之上，而借贷至今仍是一个许诺。

normal.en: German borgen and Dutch borgen are relatives that cover borrowing and lending.

normal.en: A word taken from another language is called a borrowing because it never goes back.
normal.cn: 从另一种语言取来的词叫借词，因为它再也不会归还。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with from, money, book and idea.

normal.en: Spell b-o-r-r-o-w; the double r keeps the vowel short.

abstract.en: See a hand take a book and promise to bring it back next week: that is borrow.

abstract.en: Stretch the same promise to money or to a word, and the word still fits.
abstract.cn: 把同一个许诺延伸到钱或一个词，这个词仍然适用。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the returned book bring the sense back.

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of borrow rest on one picture: taking something for a time under a promise to give it back.
sensesIntro.cn: borrow 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：在一段期限内拿走某物，并许诺归还。

branches.en: THE WORD: languages take words from each other and never give them back.
branches.cn: 词语线：语言互相取用词语，而且从不归还。

senses.title: The team game of kicking a ball
senses.definition: a game between two teams who try to kick or carry a ball into a goal
senses.definitionCN: 两队争相把球踢入或带入对方球门的运动
senses.example: Football is popular in every country.
senses.exampleCN: 足球在各国都很流行。

senses.why: The game's name was lent to the thing it is played with.

senses.title: American football
senses.definition: in America, the rough team game played with an oval ball
senses.definitionCN: 美国用椭圆形球进行的强对抗团队运动
senses.example: American football stars wear helmets.
senses.exampleCN: 美式橄榄球明星戴头盔。
senses.why: The same name followed the ball to a rougher cousin game.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名字随着球传到了更粗犷的兄弟运动。

intro.en: Football simply names a ball played with the feet.
intro.cn: football 的构词很直白：用脚踢的球。

items.en: Middle English records foteballe for folk games of kicking a ball.
items.cn: 中古英语记载 foteballe，指民间踢球游戏。

items.en: Medieval English villages played rival teams across whole fields, often banned by kings.
items.cn: 中世纪英格兰村镇常举行全场对抗，屡遭王室禁令。

items.en: Ball itself is an ancient Old English word, feallan-related by old theories of bouncing.
items.cn: ball 本身是古老的古英语词，旧理论曾把它与弹跳的 feallan 相联系。

items.en: Modern English fixed football for the codified game after schools wrote rules in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪学校制定规则后，football 指称规范化赛事。

items.en: America split the name: soccer for kicking, football for the oval-ball game.
items.cn: 美国把名称分流：踢的叫 soccer，椭圆球的叫 football。

note.en: Football belongs to a large -ball family; compare the games.
note.cn: football 属于庞大的 -ball 词族，可比较各项运动。

definition_zh: 大声地；响亮地；强烈地；花哨地
definition_en: in a way that makes a strong sound; also in an insistent or showy manner
core_image: 一个人站上台阶，张开嘴高声呼喊，声音一圈圈扩散到街角
scene: 排练室的门半开着，歌声和鼓点一阵高过一阵，楼上的住户都听见了。 The choir sang loudly enough to carry through the whole building.
sceneCN: 这里 loudly 是「大声地、响亮地」（第 1 个义项）；句意为合唱团唱得足够响，声音传遍了整栋楼。画面里可认出半开的门、谱架和排练室。

pos.zh: 大声地；响亮地；强烈地；花哨地

derivatives.zh: 由 loudly 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「响亮的；大声的」
由 loud 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「响亮；音量」
由 loud 与 mouth 复合而成，义为「爱吹嘘、话多的人」

senses.title: At a high volume of sound
senses.definition: in a way that produces a strong, easily heard sound
senses.definitionCN: 以发出强烈、容易听见的声音的方式
senses.example: She called loudly for help from the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 她在阳台上大声呼救。
senses.why: Loud comes from an old word for a strong sound, and -ly turns that quality into the way an action is done.
senses.whyCN: loud 来自表示强烈声响的古词，后缀 -ly 把这种性质变成了做动作的方式。

senses.title: With insistence, so as to be heard or noticed
senses.definition: in a forceful and public way, so that an opinion or complaint cannot be ignored
senses.definitionCN: 以有力而公开的方式，使某种意见或抱怨无法被忽视
senses.example: The residents protested loudly against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们大声抗议这条新路。
senses.why: If a sound is loud, it reaches many ears; the word therefore moves from volume to public pressure.
senses.whyCN: 声音如果响亮，就能传到很多耳朵里；因此这个词从音量转到公开施压。

senses.title: In a showy or garish manner
senses.definition: in a style that is too bright, bold or decorated to be quiet or tasteful
senses.definitionCN: 以过于鲜亮、大胆或繁复装饰、毫不含蓄的风格
senses.example: The room was loudly decorated with gold curtains and red walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间用金色窗帘和红色墙面装饰得十分扎眼。
senses.why: A loud colour or pattern, like a loud sound, refuses to stay in the background, so the word extends from hearing to sight.
senses.whyCN: 花哨的颜色或图案就像响亮的声音一样不肯退到背景里，于是这个词从听觉延伸到视觉。

intro.en: Loudly is simply loud plus the adverb suffix -ly; loud itself goes back to an Old English word for a strong sound.
intro.cn: loudly 就是 loud 加上副词后缀 -ly；loud 本身可追溯到古英语中表示强烈声响的词。

items.en: The adjective hlūd meant loud or noisy, and it described both voices and the roar of a crowd.
items.cn: 形容词 hlūd 意为响亮的、喧闹的，既形容人声，也形容人群的轰鸣。

items.en: Its reconstructed ancestor is hlūdaz, a form rebuilt from comparison with related Germanic languages.
items.cn: 其重构祖形为 hlūdaz，这个形式是通过与相关日耳曼语言比较重建出来的。

items.en: Generally the word is traced to a root meaning to hear, which also stands behind Latin words for being renowned.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词可追溯到表示「听见」的词根，拉丁语中表示「有名」的词也出自此处。

items.en: Middle English kept loud, and speakers added -ly to make an adverb of manner.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 loud，说话者加 -ly 构成方式副词。

items.en: Modern English loudly covers high volume, insistent public speech and showy appearance.
items.cn: 现代英语的 loudly 涵盖高音量、公开坚持的表达以及花哨的外观。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the loud root or are easily confused with loudly; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs of sound and manner.
note.cn: 形近组收共用 loud 词根或容易与 loudly 混淆的词；近义组收其他表示声音与方式的副词。

entries.definitionCN: 意为发出强烈声响的形容词。

entries.definitionCN: 以能被听见的声音，而非默读。

entries.definition: The quality or level of being loud.

entries.definitionCN: 被允许的；只是拼写与读音和 loudly 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: In a way that makes a lot of noise.
entries.definitionCN: 以制造大量噪声的方式。

entries.definition: With loud and forceful speech.

In a quiet and gentle way.

normalIntro.en: The word is a transparent build: loud plus -ly. Its hooks therefore come from the root for sound, the suffix, and the way loud spreads from hearing to behaviour.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的构造很透明：loud 加 -ly。记忆钩子因此来自表示声音的词根、后缀，以及 loud 从听觉扩展到行为的方式。

normal.en: Loudly is loud plus -ly, so the meaning is simply in a loud way.
normal.cn: loudly 是 loud 加 -ly，意思就是「以响亮的方式」。

normal.en: The older form hlūd already meant noisy, so the word has been about sound for a long time.
normal.cn: 更早的形式 hlūd 已经表示喧闹，所以这个词长期都与声音有关。

normal.en: Aloud uses the same root but means out loud rather than in a loud way.
normal.cn: aloud 用同一词根，但意思是「出声地」，而不是「大声地」。

normal.en: The comparative is more loudly, not loudlier, because the word already ends in -ly.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more loudly，而不是 loudlier，因为这个词本身已以 -ly 结尾。

normal.en: Loudly can follow protest and complain, where the volume is social pressure rather than decibels.
normal.cn: loudly 可以跟 protest、complain 搭配，此时「响」是社交压力而不是分贝。

abstract.en: A sound that is loud pushes into other people's space, and the adverb carries that same push into protest.
abstract.cn: 响亮的声音会挤进别人的空间，这个副词把同样的推力带进了抗议。

abstract.en: The move from a loud voice to a loud shirt shows that English treats both as things that refuse to be ignored.
abstract.cn: 从响亮的嗓音到花哨的衬衫，说明英语把两者都看成不肯被忽视的东西。

abstract.en: Adding -ly to a quality is like turning a colour into a way of painting: loud becomes the manner of the action.
abstract.cn: 给一种性质加 -ly，就像把颜色变成画法：loud 变成了动作的方式。

examples.en: She called loudly for help from the balcony.
examples.cn: 她在阳台上大声呼救。

examples.en: The choir sang loudly enough to carry through the whole building.
examples.cn: 合唱团唱得足够响，声音传遍了整栋楼。

definition_zh: 对面的；相反的；对立的；对立面；对手；在…对面
definition_en: placed on the other side of something and facing it, or completely different and contrary in nature; as a noun, the person, thing or word that stands against another; as a preposition, across from
core_image: 一条窄街两侧正对着的两扇窗，一边亮着灯，一边漆黑
scene: 雨后的窄街两侧，两扇窗正对着，一边亮着暖黄的灯，一边漆黑。 The two houses stand opposite each other across the narrow street.
sceneCN: 这里 opposite 是「在…对面」（第 3 个义项：介词，处在另一侧）；句意为两栋房子隔着窄街相对而立，画面是雨后小街与两扇正对的窗。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 opponere 经法语进入英语，义为「反对；对抗」
由 oppose 加名词后缀 -ition 构成，义为「反对；对立；反对党」
由拉丁语 opponere 的现在分词词干加 -ent 构成，义为「对手；反对者」
由 oppose 加 -ing 构成，义为「对立的；反对的」

senses.title: Facing across from another
senses.definition: placed on the other side of something, so that the two sides look towards each other
senses.definitionCN: 处在某物的另一侧，两者正面相对
senses.example: The shop is on the opposite side of the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店在路的对面。
senses.why: Latin ob- means against or facing, and ponere means to place, so oppositus is literally placed facing something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ob- 表示「对着、面向」，ponere 表示「放置」，所以 oppositus 字面就是「被放成面对面」；这个义项说的正是空间上正对的那一侧。

senses.title: Completely different or contrary
senses.definition: very different from something else, especially so that the two cannot both be true or both be chosen
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物极为不同，尤指两者不能同时成立或同时选择
senses.example: Her account of the evening was the opposite of his.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那晚的说法和他的完全相反。
senses.why: Two things placed face to face look in contrary directions, so the picture of facing turns into the idea of contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 两个东西一旦面对面摆好，朝向就是相反的；「相对而立」的画面于是转成「说法、性质彼此相反」的抽象意义，重点从位置移到矛盾。

senses.title: Across from; facing
senses.definition: in a position on the other side of something and directly facing it
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的另一侧，并正对着它
senses.example: She sat opposite me at the small table.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在小桌子对面，正对着我。
senses.why: The preposition freezes the spatial picture: two things placed against each other with a gap between them, and the word only names the position.
senses.whyCN: 介词用法把这个空间画面固定下来：两样东西隔着一段距离互相对着；此时词只负责指出位置，不再涉及抽象的对立。

senses.title: The person or thing set against another
senses.definition: a person or thing that is as different as possible from another, or a word that expresses the contrary
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人或物差异最大的一方，也指表示相反意思的词
senses.example: In the debate, the two speakers were exact opposites.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论中，两位发言人的立场截然相反。
senses.why: Once the adjective names the far side, it can stand alone as a noun for whatever occupies that far side.
senses.whyCN: 既然形容词能指「远的那一侧」，它就可以单独作名词，指占据那一侧的人、物或词；从描述位置转为指称实体。

intro.en: Opposite comes from Latin opponere, to place against, and its history is first physical: things put face to face before ideas could be in conflict.
intro.cn: opposite 出自拉丁语 opponere（放在对面），它的历史先是物理的：先有面对面摆放的东西，才有互相冲突的观念。

items.en: Ob- meant against or towards and ponere meant to place, so opponere was to set one thing in front of another.
items.cn: ob- 表示「对着、朝向」，ponere 表示「放置」，所以 opponere 就是把一样东西摆到另一样的前面。

items.en: The past participle oppositus described something placed facing another thing, and it kept both the position and the contrast.
items.cn: 过去分词 oppositus 形容被摆成面对另一物的事物，既保留位置，也带出对比。

items.en: Old French took the Latin participle as opposite, meaning placed on the other side, and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把这一拉丁分词写作 opposite，意为「位于另一侧的」，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English used opposite as an adjective for facing things and as a noun for the side that faces us.
items.cn: 中古英语里 opposite 既作形容词指「相对而立的」，也作名词指「正对着我们的那一方」。

items.en: Modern English adds the preposition use from the eighteenth century and extends the adjective from space to ideas that contradict each other.
items.cn: 现代英语在十八世纪补上介词用法，并把形容词从空间上的相对扩展到互相矛盾的观点。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin verb for placing against; the near-meaning group gathers words for facing positions and contrary senses.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「放在对面」这一动词上的词；近义组收表示面对的位置与相反意义的词。

entries.definition: To act against something or to say that it is wrong.

entries.definitionCN: 反对的行为，也指反对的一方。

entries.definition: A person who competes against or argues against another.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一人竞争或争论的对手。

entries.definition: Suitable and well placed in relation to the matter at hand; the spelling resembles opposite but the prefix changes the sense to fitting.
entries.definitionCN: 恰当而切题的；拼写与 opposite 相近，前缀不同，侧重「贴合」。

entries.definition: Opposite in direction or in nature.
The exact contrary of what has been stated or done.
entries.definitionCN: 所述或所做之事的正相反一面。

entries.definition: Positioned so as to look towards something.
On the other side of something and directly facing it.
entries.definitionCN: 在某物的另一侧并正对着它。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a prefix meaning against and a verb meaning to place, so every hook returns to something set down face to face.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「对着」的前缀与表示「放置」的动词构成，所有记忆钩子都回到「面对面摆下」这个动作。

normal.en: Opposite is ob- plus ponere, against plus to place, so the first picture is two objects set down facing each other.
normal.cn: opposite 是 ob- 加 ponere，也就是「对着」加「放置」，最早的画面是两件东西面对面摆好。

normal.en: Oppose keeps the verb alive: to put oneself against something, which is why opposition grows from the same stem.
normal.cn: oppose 保留了动词义：把自己摆到某事对面，所以 opposition 从同一词干长出来。

normal.en: The adjective can become a noun because the far side can be named without saying what it is far from.
normal.cn: 形容词能变成名词，因为「远的那一侧」可以不给参照物就直接被指出来。

normal.en: Opposite side and opposite direction still measure space, while the opposite of measures ideas.
normal.cn: opposite side 与 opposite direction 仍在量空间，the opposite of 则在量想法。

normal.en: English says opposite the bank without a preposition, because the word already carries the across idea inside it.
normal.cn: 英语说 opposite the bank 时不加介词，因为这个词本身已经含有「横过、对面」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture two windows on a narrow street, each lit from within, each facing the other; that pair is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 想象窄街两侧的两扇窗，各自从里面亮着，各自正对另一边；这一对窗就是这个词的全部。

abstract.en: Two arrows painted on a road point in contrary ways, and that is how a position becomes a contradiction.
abstract.cn: 路面上画着的两支箭头指向相反，位置上的相对就是这样变成了意义上的矛盾。

abstract.en: Two people across a small table can disagree without moving, and opposite is the gap that holds them apart.
abstract.cn: 隔着张小桌的两个人可以不动地方就彼此不同意，而 opposite 正是把他们隔开的那段距离。

senses.whyCN: 最古老的画面是有边界的开阔土地：被派上用场的地。

intro.en: Field is an ancient Germanic word for open or cleared land, sharing a root with the idea of flat ground.
intro.cn: field 是表示开阔或开垦土地的古老日耳曼词，与「平地」概念同根。

items.en: A reconstructed root felthuz meant 'flat land, plain'; Dutch veld and German Feld are cousins.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 felthuz 意为「平地、平原」；荷兰语 veld 与德语 Feld 是同族词。

items.en: Old English feld meant 'open land, plain without woods', next to cleared ground.
items.cn: 古英语 feld 意为「旷野、无林平地」，与垦地相邻。

items.en: Middle English used field for farmland, battlefields and open country alike.
items.cn: 中古英语用 field 兼指农田、战场与旷野。

items.en: The word spread to sports grounds and branches of knowledge.
items.cn: 现代英语将其扩展到运动场与学问分支。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics borrowed field for regions of magnetic and gravitational force.
items.cn: 十九世纪物理学借 field 指磁场与引力场所在的区域。

note.en: Look-alikes differ by one letter; near-meaning words cover land, domains and playing grounds.
note.cn: 形近组仅差一个字母；近义组覆盖土地、领域与运动场地。

items.cn: 现代英语把 huge 扩展到数量、成就与重要性。

definition_zh: 钦佩；赞赏；欣赏；仰慕
definition_en: to think highly of someone or something, or to enjoy looking at it

scene: 画展上，同学们围着作品连声赞叹。 They admired the painting for a long time.

senses.title: To think highly of someone
senses.definition: to respect a person and think well of them
senses.definitionCN: 敬重某人并看好他
senses.example: We admire her courage.
senses.exampleCN: 我们钦佩她的勇气。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to wonder at, and wondering at a person turns into respect and admiration.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「对……惊叹」，对一个人惊叹，就转为敬重与钦佩。

senses.title: To enjoy looking at something
senses.definition: to look at something with pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 愉快地观看某物
senses.example: They admired the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 他们欣赏那座老桥。
senses.why: Wonder can also be felt before a beautiful thing, which gives the sense of enjoying a view or an object.
senses.whyCN: 惊叹也可以落在美好的事物上，于是有了欣赏某物的意思。

senses.title: To praise someone
senses.definition: to speak with praise about a person
senses.definitionCN: 带着赞美谈论某人
senses.example: The teacher admired his neat work.
senses.exampleCN: 老师称赞他整洁的作业。
senses.why: Wondering aloud becomes praise, so admire can mean speaking well of someone.
senses.whyCN: 把惊叹说出口，就变成称赞某人。

senses.title: To look at a view
senses.definition: to stand and look at a wide view
senses.definitionCN: 停下来观看开阔的景色
senses.example: We stopped to admire the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 我们停下来观赏大海。
senses.why: Stopping to let the eyes rest on a wide view is the act of admiring a scene.
senses.whyCN: 停下脚步让目光停在开阔的景色上，就是观赏。

senses.title: The object of a verb
senses.definition: the pronoun a speaker uses when referring to himself or herself as the direct or indirect object of a verb
senses.definitionCN: 说话人指自己、充当动词直接或间接宾语时用的代词
senses.example: The teacher asked me a difficult question.
senses.exampleCN: 老师问了我一个难题。
senses.why: Old English kept a separate accusative form mē for the object role, so the pronoun changes shape the moment it stops being the subject.
senses.whyCN: 古英语为宾语角色保留了独立的宾格形式 mē，所以这个代词一旦不做主语就得换形，me 正是那套格变化留下的宾语形态。

senses.title: The object of a preposition
senses.definition: the pronoun used after a preposition when the speaker is the thing the preposition points to
senses.definitionCN: 介词之后使用、表示介词所指向的说话人本身的代词
senses.example: This letter is addressed to me.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信是寄给我的。
senses.why: Old English prepositions governed the dative, and the same mē served both object cases, which is why one short form now covers every preposition.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的介词支配与格，而同一个 mē 同时承担两种宾语格，所以今天一个短形式就能跟在所有介词后面。

senses.title: The complement after be
senses.definition: the pronoun used after a linking verb or in a comparison, where older grammar once expected the subject form
senses.definitionCN: 连系动词之后或比较句中使用的代词，旧语法在此处本要求用主格
senses.example: It was me at the door, not my brother.
senses.exampleCN: 在门口的是我，不是我弟弟。
senses.why: After be the pronoun is felt as the point of focus rather than the doer, so the object form survives where Latin-based rules would still ask for the subject form.
senses.whyCN: 在 be 之后，代词被感知为被指出的焦点而不是动作发出者，因此在依拉丁规则本该用主格的位置，宾格形式反而留了下来。

senses.title: The subject in informal speech
senses.definition: the pronoun used as part of the subject in casual speech, especially when it is joined to another noun by and
senses.definitionCN: 随意口语中充当主语一部分的代词，尤指与另一个名词用 and 并列时
senses.example: Me and my cousin run a small shop.
senses.exampleCN: 我和我表弟经营一家小店。
senses.why: In relaxed speech the pronoun is treated as one unmarked word rather than as a case form, so me spreads into the subject slot that school grammar reserves for I.
senses.whyCN: 在随意的口语里，代词被当成一个不带格标记的词，于是 me 扩散到学校语法留给 I 的主语位置。

intro.en: Me is the old object form of the first person pronoun, and it descends from a root shared by Latin and English.
intro.cn: me 是第一人称代词古老的宾语形式，其词根为拉丁语与英语所共有。

items.en: A reconstructed first person root *me- supplied the oblique forms of the pronoun in many branches of the family.
items.cn: 重构的第一人称词根 *me- 为这一语族许多分支提供了代词的斜格形式。

items.en: The accusative *mek and the dative *miz stood behind the single Old English form that English later kept.
items.cn: 宾格 *mek 与与格 *miz 共同支撑了古英语那个后来被英语保留下来的单一形式。

items.en: Old English mē served as both accusative and dative of ic, the word for I.
items.cn: 古英语 mē 同时充当 ic（我）的宾格与与格。

items.en: Middle English kept me while the old case system slowly broke down and word order took over the work of marking roles.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了 me，同时旧的格系统逐渐瓦解，标记句子角色的工作转由词序承担。

items.en: Modern English uses me for every object role and, informally, for subjects and complements as well.
items.cn: 现代英语用 me 承担所有宾语角色，口语中还扩展到主语与表语。

normalIntro.en: The word survives from a pronoun paradigm that once marked case on every form; its nearest relatives are the other first person forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自一套曾为每个形式标格的代词体系，它最近的亲属就是第一人称的其他形式。

normal.en: Old English had ic for the subject and mē for the object, and English kept the second form as me.
normal.cn: 古英语用 ic 作主语、mē 作宾语，英语把后者留成了 me。

normal.en: The same m- stem runs through my, mine and myself, so all of them point back to the speaker.
normal.cn: 同一个 m- 词干贯穿 my、mine 与 myself，它们都指回说话人。

normal.en: Latin mē is the same pronoun, so the resemblance is not a coincidence but a shared inheritance.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mē 是同一个代词，所以这种相似不是巧合，而是共同的继承。

normal.en: After a preposition English almost always wants me rather than I, because the object case survived longest there.
normal.cn: 在介词后面英语几乎总是用 me 而不是 I，因为宾格在那里存留得最久。

normal.en: Excuse me is a fixed phrase, so the object form stays even though no verb follows it.
normal.cn: excuse me 是固定短语，所以后面没有动词时也仍然用宾格形式。

abstract.en: Think of me as the version of I that other people can act upon: it appears when something is done to the speaker.
abstract.cn: 把 me 想成可以被别人施加动作的那个 I：当有事情落到说话人身上时，它就出现。

abstract.en: A pronoun is a placeholder, and me is the smallest label a speaker can attach to a body in a room.
abstract.cn: 代词是占位符，而 me 是说话人能贴到房间里某具身体上的最小标签。

abstract.en: A single letter m carries the speaker across languages, from English me to Latin mē.
abstract.cn: 一个字母 m 就把说话人带过语言的边界，从英语 me 到拉丁语 mē。

definition_zh: 开始；着手；起始于；起初是
definition_en: to start doing something, or to start to happen or exist
core_image: 起跑线上，第一只脚刚刚踏出去
scene: 操场上，体育老师吹响哨子，学生们同时从起跑线出发。 The race begins when the whistle blows.
sceneCN: 这里 begin 是「开始」（第 1 个义项：某事开始发生）；句意为哨声一响，比赛就开始了。

senses.title: To start doing something
senses.definition: to take the first step in an action, often followed by to do or doing
senses.definitionCN: 在某项行动中迈出第一步，后面常接 to do 或 doing
senses.example: She began to read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她开始读那封信。
senses.why: Old English beginnan joined be-, which sets about, with ginnan, to begin, so the verb literally means to set about an action.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 beginnan 由表「着手」的 be- 与表「开始」的 ginnan 组成，所以这个动词字面就是「着手做一件事」。

senses.title: For an event to start
senses.definition: for an event, period, or process to start, with no person doing the action
senses.definitionCN: 指事件、时段或过程自己开始，没有人去执行动作
senses.example: The film begins at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 电影七点开始。
senses.why: When nothing is being begun, the same verb keeps the first-step image but the subject is the event itself, so begin means simply to start happening.
senses.whyCN: 当没有谁去「开始」什么时，这个动词保留「第一步」的画面，但主语变成了事件本身，于是 begin 就只表示「开始发生」。

senses.title: To have something as a starting point
senses.definition: to start with a particular thing, place, or detail, often in begin with
senses.definitionCN: 以某事物、某处或某细节为开端，常用于 begin with 结构
senses.example: The story begins with a letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事以一封信开头。
senses.why: A first step needs a point to step from, and begin with names exactly that point, so the verb can mean to take something as the starting place.
senses.whyCN: 第一步总得有个落脚点，begin with 正是把这个落脚点点明，于是动词可以表示「以某物为起点」。

senses.title: To be at first
senses.definition: to exist at first in a particular form, before later changing
senses.definitionCN: 最初以某种形态存在，之后再发生变化
senses.example: The club began as a small reading group.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部起初只是一个小读书会。
senses.why: Push the first step back to the very earliest stage and it describes what something was at its start, which is the sense of beginning as something.
senses.whyCN: 把「第一步」一直往前推到最早的阶段，就变成描述某物开头时的样子，这就是「起初是某种事物」的义项。

intro.en: Begin is an old English compound verb that kept an irregular past tense.
intro.cn: begin 是古老的英语复合动词，保留了不规则的过去式。

items.en: Old English beginnan meant to start or to attempt, and it was already a compound verb.
items.cn: 古英语 beginnan 意为「开始、着手尝试」，当时已是复合动词。

items.en: The first element be- added the idea of setting about or going at something.
items.cn: 第一个成分 be- 增添了「着手、对着某物去」的意思。

items.en: The second element ginnan meant to begin, and it now survives only inside this verb and its forms.
items.cn: 第二个成分 ginnan 意为「开始」，今天只存活在这个动词及其形式里。

items.en: The verb kept an old strong pattern, so the past is began and the participle is begun instead of regular -ed forms.
items.cn: 这个动词保留了古老的强变化，因此过去式是 began、过去分词是 begun，而不是规则的 -ed 形式。

items.en: Middle English kept the verb and added the noun beginning, and the meaning stayed close to starting.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个动词，并加出名词 beginning，词义一直贴近「开始」。

items.en: Today begin covers actions, events and origins, while start is the more common verb in everyday speech.
items.cn: 今天 begin 可指动作、事件和起源，而日常口语中 start 更为常用。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of begin keeps the first-step picture: a person starts an action, an event starts itself, a thing is the starting point, or the earliest stage is named.

senses.example: He swung at the ball but missed it completely.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝球挥棒，却完全没打中。
senses.why: Old English missan described a shot or a blow that went wide of its mark, and that physical failure to connect is the picture every later sense keeps borrowing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 missan 最早说的是一箭或一击偏了靶心、没能碰上目标；这种身体上「没接上」的画面，是后面每个义项一直在借用的起点。

senses.title: To be too late for a train, bus or chance
senses.definition: to arrive too late for a bus, train or opportunity, so that it is lost
senses.definitionCN: 到达得太晚，没能赶上公交、火车或机会，于是失去它
senses.example: We ran for the platform but missed the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 我们朝站台跑过去，却错过了最后一班火车。
senses.why: A train leaves on its own timetable, so missing it repeats the same failure to connect, now measured in minutes rather than in inches.
senses.whyCN: 列车按自己的时刻表开走，「错过」还是那次没接上，只是衡量的尺度从几寸变成了几分钟，于是同一个词从靶场挪到了站台。

senses.title: To feel sad because someone is absent
senses.definition: to feel unhappy because a person or thing you care about is not with you
senses.definitionCN: 因为牵挂的人或物不在身边而感到难过
senses.example: She missed her family more than she had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 她想念家人的程度超出了自己的预料。
senses.why: Since missan could also mean to be without something, the verb could name the ache of that absence; the target you fail to reach becomes a person you fail to keep near.
senses.whyCN: 既然 missan 还能表示「身边没有某物」，这个词就可以指那份缺席带来的空落；没能击中的目标，变成了没能守在身边的人。

senses.title: To notice that something is not there
senses.definition: to notice that a thing or person is no longer in its usual place
senses.definitionCN: 察觉到某物或某人已不在原来的位置
senses.example: I missed my wallet only when I reached the till.
senses.exampleCN: 直到走到收银台，我才发现钱包不见了。
senses.why: A hand still reaches for the pocket where the wallet always sits, and the empty place is what the eye reports; the sense turns absence into a small act of noticing.
senses.whyCN: 手仍按老习惯伸向总放钱包的口袋，眼睛报告的是那块空处；这一层把「缺少」变成了一个察觉的动作。

senses.title: A title for an unmarried woman
senses.definition: a title placed before the surname of an unmarried woman, or used in direct address
senses.definitionCN: 放在未婚女子姓氏之前、或用于当面称呼的称谓
senses.example: Miss Adams teaches the youngest class.
senses.exampleCN: 亚当斯小姐教年纪最小的那个班。
senses.why: This title is a different word altogether, a shortened form of mistress, which once meant a woman in charge; as mistress narrowed, the clipped form kept only the neutral address, which is why it merely looks like the verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓其实是另一个词：mistress 的缩略，本指「掌家的女人」；后来 mistress 词义收窄，缩略形式只留下中性的称呼，所以它只是碰巧和动词长得一样。

intro.en: Miss is a Germanic verb for going wide of a mark; it reached English before the Norman conquest, and a separate word later shrank into the title Miss.
intro.cn: miss 是日耳曼语中表示「偏出目标」的动词，在诺曼征服之前就进入英语；另有一个与它无关的词后来缩略成了称谓 Miss。

items.en: The reconstructed form *missijan- meant to go wrong or to fail to reach, and it is the common ancestor of the Germanic verbs of missing.
items.cn: *missijan- 是重构形式，意为「走岔、没能到达」，是日耳曼语各语支里「错过」类动词的共同祖先。

items.en: Old English missan meant to fail to hit or reach something, and it could also mean to be without it.
items.cn: 古英语 missan 意为没能击中或到达某物，也可以指身边没有它。

items.en: Middle English kept both strands alive: failing to hit a target and lacking something that ought to be there.
items.cn: 中古英语把两条线都留着：既指没打中目标，也指缺了本该有的东西。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb was used for feeling a person's absence, while the noun a miss named a shot that went wide.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已经用来表示感到某人不在身边；名词 a miss 则指打偏的一击。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb for targets, timetables and absent people; the title Miss is a shortening of mistress, a different word that merely looks the same.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个动词负责目标、时刻表与缺席的人；称谓 Miss 是 mistress 的缩略，来历不同，只是碰巧长得一样。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived form and the shared mis- prefix, including a word that only borrows the prefix; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of losing, skipping and failing to notice.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与共用的 mis- 前缀，也包括只借了前缀的词；近义组收表示失去、跳过与没留意的动词。

entries.definition: The present participle of miss used as an adjective: not in the expected place.
entries.definitionCN: miss 的现在分词转作形容词，指不在原处；缺失的。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning wrongly or badly, the same sideways idea that lives inside miss.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「错误地、不当」的前缀，和 miss 里那股「偏了」的意味一脉相承。

entries.definition: A wrong act or judgement; it uses mis- but its stem comes from Norse taka, so it is no relative of miss.
entries.definitionCN: 错误的行为或判断；它用了 mis- 前缀，但词干来自北欧语的 taka，与 miss 并非同族。

entries.definition: To spell a word wrongly; built from mis- and spell, with no link to the verb beyond the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 把单词拼错；由 mis- 加 spell 构成，除前缀外与动词 miss 没有关系。

entries.definition: To no longer have something, often because it slips away.
entries.definitionCN: 不再拥有某物，常因它溜走而失去。

entries.definition: To leave something out or stay away from it on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意略过某事或不去参加。

entries.definition: To fail to notice something that is there in plain view.
entries.definitionCN: 没能注意到就摆在眼前的东西。

entries.definition: To want someone or something very much, especially someone who is absent.
entries.definitionCN: 非常渴望某人或某物，尤指不在身边的人。

normalIntro.en: The verb began as an arrow going wide of its mark, and the whole family keeps that sideways step in view.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词从一支偏出靶心的箭开始，整个词族始终盯着那一步「偏到一边」。

normal.en: Old English missan already meant to go wide of a mark, so every sense begins with a shot that does not land.
normal.cn: 古英语 missan 本就说「偏了靶心」，所以每个义项都从一支没落地的箭开始。

normal.en: The prefix mis- carries the same sideways idea, which is why mistake and misspell both describe a step to the wrong side.
normal.cn: 前缀 mis- 带着同样的「偏到一边」的意味，所以 mistake 与 misspell 都描述走错一步。

normal.en: Miss the bus keeps the archery picture alive: the bus was the mark, and you arrived after it moved.
normal.cn: miss the bus 把射箭的画面留着：车就是靶，你到的时候它已经走了。

normal.en: Missing adds -ing and turns the failure into a state: what is missing is simply not where it belongs.
normal.cn: missing 加 -ing，把「没打中」变成一种状态：missing 的东西就是不在它该在的地方。

normal.en: The title Miss is a clipped mistress, a completely separate word, so it carries no sense of failing to hit anything.
normal.cn: 称谓 Miss 是 mistress 的缩略，完全是另一个词，所以它跟「没打中」毫无关系。

abstract.en: A word that starts with an arrow in the air ends up naming the ache of an empty room, which shows how far one failure can travel.
abstract.cn: 一个从空中飞箭开始的词，最后指称空房间里的那种酸楚，说明一次「没碰上」能走多远。

abstract.en: Missing a train and missing a person both leave a gap where something should have been.
abstract.cn: 错过一班车和想念一个人，都在本该有东西的位置留下空白。

abstract.en: The title sitting beside the verb is a reminder that identical shapes can hide unrelated histories.
abstract.cn: 同一个拼写旁边站着动词和称谓，提醒人：相同的形状可以藏着毫不相干的来历。

examples.en: He reached for the ball and missed it by a finger.
examples.cn: 他伸手去接球，只差一指没接住。

examples.en: I missed the early bus and walked to school.
examples.cn: 我错过了早班车，只好走去学校。

examples.en: She missed her brother most on quiet evenings.
examples.cn: 安静的傍晚，她最想念哥哥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「觅思」——想「觅」却只能「思」，正是错过与想念的滋味。

root: 古英语 missan（没击中、没到达），属日耳曼语族，更早为重构形式 *missijan-（走岔）；与拉丁语 mittere 并非同源，只是形近。称谓 Miss 另出 mistress 的缩略。

sensesIntro.en: The physical failure to hit comes first; the senses then move to a timetable, to a person who is absent, to a gap noticed in a pocket, and finally to a title that merely shares the spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是身体上没击中；义项接着走向时刻表、走向不在身边的人、走向口袋里的空处，最后走向一个只是碰巧同形的称谓。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow passing the edge of the target while the centre stays empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭擦着靶边飞过，靶心还空着。

branches.en: a bat swinging past a ball and finding only air
branches.cn: 球棒挥过球旁，只扫到空气

branches.en: a platform gate closing just before a late runner
branches.cn: 站台门在迟到者面前合拢

branches.en: an empty chair kept for someone far away
branches.cn: 为远方的人留着的一把空椅

branches.en: a hand patting a pocket where the wallet should be
branches.cn: 手拍向本该放钱包的口袋

branches.en: a classroom door with a surname written on it
branches.cn: 教室门上写着一个姓氏

intro.en: The word rests on an Old English verb of going wide, the prefix mis-, and a set of English endings that build new forms and relatives.
intro.cn: 这个词靠一个表示「偏出」的古英语动词、前缀 mis-，以及一组造出新形式与同族词的英语词尾支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for miss; the word belongs to the Germanic branch, and the similar-looking Latin mittere is a false friend.
latinIntro.cn: miss 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它属于日耳曼语这一支，形似的拉丁语 mittere 只是一个假朋友。

items.meaning: to fail to hit, to go wrong

definition_zh: 不同地；相异地；以不同的方式
definition_en: in a way that is not the same as another way
core_image: 两条岔开的小路：同一件事走出两种走法
scene: 老师说每个人解题的思路都可以不一样。 Everyone solves the maths problem differently, and that is okay.
sceneCN: 这里 differently 是「不同地」（第 1 个义项：方式不一样）；句意是每个人解题方式都不同，这没关系。

derivatives.zh: different 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不同的」的副词形式
different 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「差异；不同」
同源动词，义为「不同；相异」
加前缀 in-（不），义为「漠不关心的」

senses.title: In a way that is not the same
senses.definition: in a manner that is not the same as something else
senses.definitionCN: 以与别的方式不一样的方式
senses.example: We all learn differently, so find your own way to study.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学习方式各不相同，所以要找到适合自己的方法。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective different into a manner word, so the core image is two paths that split apart.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词 different 变成方式词，核心意象是两条岔开的小路。

senses.title: In a changed manner
senses.titleCN: 换了方式地；改变做法地
senses.definition: in a way that is not the usual or old way
senses.definitionCN: 用不同于以往、不同于习惯的方式
senses.example: After the lesson, I began to think about failure differently.
senses.exampleCN: 上完这节课后，我开始用不同的眼光看待失败。
senses.why: When a manner word points away from the old habit, it means the path has turned, so it also covers changed ways.
senses.whyCN: 方式词一旦离开旧习惯，就说明路转向了，所以它也能表示改变后的做法。

intro.en: Differently comes from the Latin family of differ.
intro.cn: differently 来自 differ 的拉丁语词族。

items.en: The verb differre meant to carry apart or to disagree, built on dis- (apart) and ferre (to carry).
items.cn: 拉丁语 differre 意为分开携带、不一致，由 dis-（分开）加 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Old French had differer, keeping the sense of being unlike.
items.cn: 古法语有 differer，保留了「不一样」的意思。

items.en: English took the adjective different from this family in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪，英语从这个词族吸收了形容词 different。

items.en: The manner suffix -ly was added to build the adverb.
items.cn: 人们给它加上方式后缀 -ly，构成副词。

items.en: Differently is now the standard way to say a thing is done in another manner.
items.cn: 如今 differently 是表示「换个方式做」的标准说法。

note.en: These words sit around the differ family and its sound pattern.
note.cn: 这些词围绕 differ 词族及其读音模式。

entries.definition: adjective: not the same
noun: the way things are not alike
verb: to be unlike
not caring either way
hard to do, different Latin root
entries.definitionCN: 困难的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: in another way
not in the usual way
clearly in a separate way
in several different ways
separated in position or manner

normalIntro.en: Use the two-path picture and the differ family to fix the word.
normalIntro.cn: 用「两条岔路」的画面和 differ 词族来记住它。

normal.en: differently ends in -ly, so it tells how, not what.
normal.cn: differently 以 -ly 结尾，说明方式，不是说明事物。

normal.en: different is the adjective; add -ly to make the adverb.
normal.cn: different 是形容词，加 -ly 变成副词。

normal.en: Everyone learns differently, a common classroom sentence.
normal.cn: Everyone learns differently 是课堂常用句。

normal.en: differ is the verb inside the family.
normal.cn: differ 是这个词族里的动词。

normal.en: Think of two roads leaving the same gate.
normal.cn: 想两条路从同一扇门出发却越走越开。

abstract.en: Picture two walkers at a fork, each choosing a path.
abstract.cn: 想象两个走路的人站在岔路口，各自选了一条路。

abstract.en: Feel the little turn your head makes when you change your view.
abstract.cn: 体会改变看法时脑袋轻轻一转的感觉。

abstract.en: Hear two answers given in two different tones.
abstract.cn: 听两种不同语气说出的两个答案。

examples.en: The twins dress differently: one loves blue, the other loves red.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎穿得不一样：一个爱蓝色，一个爱红色。

examples.en: I used to hate running, but now I think about it differently.
examples.cn: 我以前讨厌跑步，但现在对它的看法变了。

examples.en: Try to do your homework differently and see if it is faster.
examples.cn: 换个方式写作业，看看是不是更快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「的佛恩特利」——「的」字开头提醒它是副词，佛思不同、思路不同，自然就「不同地」

root: 来自拉丁语 differre（分开携带），dis-（分开）+ ferre（携带）；形容词 different 加副词后缀 -ly 构成 differently。

sensesIntro.en: Differently points at the manner of being unlike, then at a changed way.
sensesIntro.cn: differently 先指「不一样的方式」，再引申为「改变后的做法」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths that split apart
core.cn: 核心意象：两条岔开的小路

branches.en: Doing a thing in another way
branches.cn: 用另一种方式做事

branches.en: Leaving the old habit behind
branches.cn: 告别旧习惯的做法

branches.en: From being unlike to acting unlike
branches.cn: 从「不同」到「做得不同」

branches.en: A changed view of the same thing
branches.cn: 对同一件事换了个眼光

branches.en: Two learners, two methods
branches.cn: 两个学习者，两种方法

intro.en: Differently is a base word plus the manner suffix -ly.
intro.cn: differently 由词基加方式后缀 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The differ family comes from Latin ferre, to carry.
latinIntro.cn: differ 词族来自拉丁语 ferre（携带）。

items.meaning: the amount or way of being unlike

items.example: He was indifferent to the score.

definition_zh: ……的（所属）；来自；由……构成；关于；……的量
definition_en: a preposition marking possession or belonging, the source someone or something comes from, the material a thing is made from, the subject a statement is about, and the amount contained in a measure
core_image: 一只白瓷杯里盛着热茶，杯沿上绕着一缕白气
scene: 午后的厨房很安静，炉上的水刚停，桌上摆着一只白瓷杯和几片切好的柠檬。 She poured a cup of tea and left it to cool by the window.
sceneCN: 这里的 of 是「……的量」（第 5 个义项：表示容器或单位所含的数量）；句意为她倒了一杯茶，放在窗边晾着。图中可辨识物件：白瓷杯、茶、柠檬片。

derivatives.zh: 与 of 同源，来自古英语 æf 的强调形式，义为「离开；断开」
由 of 弱化而来的构词成分，见于 offshoot 等词，表示「离开、分出」
由 there 与 of 复合而成，义为「由此；关于那一点」

senses.title: Belonging to or connected with
senses.definition: used between two nouns to show that the second belongs to, is part of, or is connected with the first
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个名词之间，表示后者属于、构成或关联于前者
senses.example: The roof of the old house leaked in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子的屋顶在暴风雨中漏了。
senses.why: Old English used the genitive ending on nouns for possession, and of, meaning 'from', gradually took over that work as endings wore away.
senses.whyCN: 古英语靠名词上的属格词尾表示所属，随着词尾逐渐磨损，意为「从……而来」的 of 慢慢接过了这项职能。

senses.title: Coming from a particular source
senses.definition: used after a noun to name the place, person or group that something comes from
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后，指出某物来自的地方、人或群体
senses.example: She is a teacher of mathematics from a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位来自小镇的数学老师。
senses.why: The earliest sense of the word was 'away from', so naming where something starts out is one of its oldest jobs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的意思是「离开、从……而来」，所以指出某物的来处是它最古老的职能之一。

senses.title: Made or consisting of a material
senses.definition: used to name the substance a thing is made from or the parts that make it up
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出某物由什么材料制成，或由哪些部分构成
senses.example: The frame is made of bamboo and the seat of woven grass.
senses.exampleCN: 框架由竹子制成，座面则由编草做成。
senses.why: Once of marks where a thing comes from, it can also mark what it was built out of, since material is a kind of origin.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 of 标出某物的来处，它也能标出某物由什么造成，因为材料也是一种来源。

senses.title: About or concerning
senses.definition: used after certain verbs and nouns to introduce the subject that is being thought, spoken or written about
senses.definitionCN: 用在某些动词和名词后，引出被思考、谈论或书写的主题
senses.example: He told us a long story of the sea and its storms.
senses.exampleCN: 他给我们讲了一个关于大海和风暴的长故事。
senses.why: To speak of something is to start from it and move outward in words, so the preposition of source became the marker of a topic.
senses.whyCN: 说到某事物，就是以它为起点用话语向外展开，于是这个表示来源的介词也成了话题的标记。

senses.title: Showing the amount contained in a measure
senses.definition: used between a quantity word or container and the thing it measures, as in a cup of tea or a piece of paper
senses.definitionCN: 用在数量词或容器与它所量的东西之间，如 a cup of tea 或 a piece of paper
senses.example: He asked for a glass of water and a slice of bread.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一杯水和一片面包。
senses.why: A measure is hollow until something fills it, so of joins the container to its contents and turns two words into one quantity.
senses.whyCN: 度量本身是空的，直到有东西把它填满，于是 of 把容器和内容连起来，让两个词合成一个数量。

intro.en: Of is one of the oldest English words, an unstressed form of a Germanic word meaning 'away from', and its modern uses grew as English lost the noun endings that once marked possession.
intro.cn: of 是英语最古老的词之一，是日耳曼语中表示「离开、从……而来」的词的非重读形式；随着英语丢掉曾经标示所属的名词词尾，它的现代用法才逐渐长成。

items.en: Scholars generally reconstruct a form meaning 'off, away from' behind this family, and the same source is thought to lie behind Greek apo and Latin ab.
items.cn: 学者一般认为这一族词背后有一个表示「离开、从……而来」的形式，并认为希腊语 apo 与拉丁语 ab 也出自同一来源。

items.en: The Germanic form carried the sense of moving away or departing, and it worked as an unstressed preposition rather than a stressed adverb.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式带着「离开、出发」的意思，且多作非重读介词，而不是重读副词。

items.en: Old English had æf, meaning away or from, alongside of as its weaker, unstressed form in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 古英语有 æf，意为「离开、从」，而 of 是它在日常口语中较弱、非重读的形式。

items.en: Middle English let of take over the possessive work of fading noun endings, so phrases like the roof of the house replaced older inflected forms.
items.cn: 中古英语让 of 接手逐渐消失的名词词尾的所属职能，于是 the roof of the house 这类说法取代了更早的屈折形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps of for possession, source, material, topic and quantity, while its stressed twin off survives as a separate word for departure.
items.cn: 现代英语让 of 承担所属、来源、材料、话题与数量，而它重读的双胞胎 off 作为表示「离开」的独立词留存下来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words whose spelling or history stands close to of; the near-meaning group collects prepositions and phrases that express possession or origin.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或来历与 of 相近的词；近义组收表示所属或来源的介词与说法。

entries.definition: Away from a place, or not switched on; the stressed twin of of.
entries.definitionCN: 离开某处，或未接通电源；of 的重读双胞胎。

entries.definition: To present something for someone to accept; the spelling is close but the source is Latin offerre, so it is not related to of.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物呈上供人接受；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自拉丁语 offerre。

entries.definition: An old poetic shortening of often, meaning many times; it is only spelling that resembles of, the source is separate.
entries.definitionCN: often 的古老诗歌缩略形式，意为「多次」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Of that or of it, a formal word built by joining there and of.
entries.definitionCN: 关于那一点或它的，由 there 与 of 合成的正式用语。

entries.definition: A preposition marking the starting point or source of something.
entries.definitionCN: 标示某物起点或来源的介词。

entries.definition: A phrase saying that something is owned by or part of another.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某物归另一物所有或属于它的说法。

entries.definition: A preposition naming the subject of speech, thought or writing.
entries.definitionCN: 引出谈话、思考或写作主题的介词。

entries.definition: A phrase saying what substance something is produced out of.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某物由何种材料制成的说法。

normalIntro.en: Of is a tiny word doing several large jobs at once, and every hook follows the one old idea of starting out from something.
normalIntro.cn: of 是个小词，却同时干着好几件大事，而每条记忆钩子都顺着「从某处出发」这个古老想法。

normal.en: Old English æf meant away or from, and of was simply its light, unstressed form in quick speech.
normal.cn: 古英语 æf 意为「离开、从」，of 只是它在快语速中轻读的形式。

normal.en: Off is the same word under stress, which is why a shop can be off a street and a lid can come off a box.
normal.cn: off 是同一个词的重读形式，所以一家店可以在街道拐出去的位置，盖子也能从盒子上取下来。

normal.en: English once put endings on nouns for possession; as those endings disappeared, of stepped in, giving the roof of the house.
normal.cn: 英语曾在名词上加词尾表示所属；这些词尾消失后，of 补了进来，于是有了 the roof of the house。

normal.en: A cup of tea joins container and contents, so the preposition turns two nouns into one measured amount.
normal.cn: a cup of tea 把容器与内容连在一起，这个介词就把两个名词合成一个被量出的数量。

normal.en: Of course, of mine and think of each freeze a different piece of grammar into a phrase worth learning whole.
normal.cn: of course、of mine 与 think of 各自把一处不同的语法冻成了值得整块记住的说法。

abstract.en: Of is the word English uses when one thing has to be anchored to another, whether by owner, origin, stuff or subject.
abstract.cn: 当一样东西必须拴到另一样上时，英语就动用 of，无论靠的是主人、来处、材料还是话题。

abstract.en: Its history shows a language quietly replacing its own grammar with a small preposition.
abstract.cn: 它的历史显示：一门语言悄悄用一个小介词替换掉了自己原有的语法。

abstract.en: A cup of tea is two nouns and a hinge, which is all most possession really is.
abstract.cn: a cup of tea 是两个名词加一个铰链，而多数「所属」其实也不过如此。

examples.en: The handle of the door came loose during the winter.
examples.cn: 门把手在冬天松动脱落了。

examples.en: She is a friend of my sister and lives in the same building.
examples.cn: 她是我姐姐的朋友，住在这栋楼里。

examples.en: They drank a pot of tea and talked until midnight.
examples.cn: 他们喝了一壶茶，一直聊到半夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「偶夫」——偶然遇到的丈夫，说起「什么东西的」；记住 of 是「……的」。

root: 古英语 æf（离开、从）的非重读形式 of；与 off 同源，一般认为与希腊语 apo、拉丁语 ab 同出原始印欧语中表示「离开」的形式。

sensesIntro.en: The core is starting out from a point; possession, source, material, topic and quantity are five ways that small movement gets used.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「从某一点出发」；所属、来源、材料、话题与数量，就是这一小段「离开」被用到的五种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white porcelain cup holding hot tea, a thread of steam curling above the rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只白瓷杯里盛着热茶，杯沿上绕着一缕白气。

branches.en: a roof that belongs to one particular old house
branches.cn: 只属于某一座老房子的屋顶

branches.en: a teacher who came out of a small town
branches.cn: 从一座小镇走出来的老师

branches.en: a frame built out of cut bamboo
branches.cn: 用截好的竹子搭成的框架

branches.en: a long story told about the sea
branches.cn: 一个关于大海的长故事

branches.en: a cup filled to the rim with hot tea
branches.cn: 倒到杯沿的热茶

intro.en: Of has no prefixes or suffixes of its own; the entries below show its Old English ancestor, its stressed twin, its Latin and Greek relatives, and the endings that once did its work.
intro.cn: of 本身没有前缀或后缀；下面列的是它的古英语祖先、重读双胞胎、拉丁与希腊亲族，以及曾经替它干活的那些词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ab is generally regarded as a cognate of this family, both going back to a reconstructed Indo-European form for 'away from'; it is listed here as a relative rather than a parent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ab 一般被认为与这一族词同源，二者都上溯到一个表示「离开」的原始印欧语重构形式；此处把它列为亲族而非祖先。
